pageCache.text:
Welcome to Herne Bay Infant and Nursery School
Herne Bay Infant and Nursery School is a local education authority maintained infant school, which sits at the heart of the community that it serves.
Our Nursery, Inkpen Class, admits children the seasonal term after their 3rd birthday.
The children join the main school in the academic year that they are 5 years old, and in the September following their 7th birthday they then move onto their parent choice of junior school. The majority of our children attend Herne Bay Junior School with whom we share linked admission arrangements.
We have 9 classes; three Year 2 classes, two Year 1 classes, three Reception and one Nursery class.
We work in close partnership with families to prepare children for school and life beyond.
All our work and relationships in school are underpinned by our school values. These are Resilience, Kindness, Ambition, Teamwork and Respect.
When you have looked at all the information available, we hope you will understand that this is a safe, happy and caring place for your child to begin an exciting journey in education.

Welcome to our Reception 2026 new starter page.
Welcome to Herne Bay Infant and Nursery School! We are delighted that your child will be joining us this year. Herne Bay Infant is a friendly and supportive school where all members of the school community work as a team to ensure your child has a positive and memorable educational experience.
Our school values are – Resilience, Respect, Kindness, Teamwork and Ambition and our children are proud to demonstrate these values every day.
We look forward to working with you and your child to ensure they achieve the very best they can and enjoy their time at Herne Bay Infant and Nursery School.

Peggy Our School Dog
You may be aware that there is a growing movement in many schools to reintroduce the concept of school pets as a way of teaching all children responsibility and providing a source of pleasure and learning.
Peggy is a Cocker Spaniel, known for being extremely good with children, intelligent and easy to train. When she was a puppy, she came into school on several occasions for us to assess her behaviour and temperament, in a school environment, and see whether she was suitable to become our school dog.
With parental permission, children are allowed to interact with Peggy under supervision from staff. We do everything we can to reassure children who are fearful and under no circumstances will they be forced to meet with her.
Whilst moving around the school, Peggy will always be on a lead with an adult who is responsible for managing her. Peggy will reside in Ms Brown and Mr Leone’s office when not with children or greeting you on the gate.
She cannot wait to meet you!

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast Club - Herne Bay Infant and Nursery School
pageCache.text:
The school provides a daily Breakfast Club that runs from 7.45am until 8.45am each morning during term time, where a healthy, nutritious breakfast is provided at a cost of £3.50 per day.
There is a daily choice of cereal, toast, fruit and yoghurt with fruit juice or milk to drink. After they have eaten, the children have an opportunity to socialise, playing with their friends and joining in with games.
Parents supply their child with a toothbrush in a named bag, so they have an opportunity to clean their teeth before the start of school.
Further information and a form to register your interest can be found here Breakfast Club Form or obtained from via the School Office.

pageCache.pageTitle: Attendance and Punctuality - Herne Bay Infant and Nursery School
pageCache.text:
School Attendance
Our School Attendance Target is 100%
Here is an example of how low attendance can impact your child –
Taylor is in Year 2. Her attendance rate is around 90%. Her family thinks this is pretty good.
So, what does an attendance rate of 90% look like?
90% attendance means that Taylor is absent for the equivalent of one half-day per week.
In Year 1 Taylor’s 90% attendance rate means that she has missed the equivalent or four whole weeks of lessons in the school year.
If Taylor continues to attend for 90% of the time that she is at primary school, she will miss a total of 23 weeks which is equivalent to over half a school year.
The school year is made up of 190 days, and there is 175 days when your child does not come into school. How much education has your child missed per year?
95% = 10 days 80% = 40 days
90% = 20 days 75% = 50 days
85% = 30 days 70% = 60 days
Acceptable reason for not being in school:
Unacceptable reasons for not being in school
Contagious diseases like chicken pox, measles, influenza, sickness, and diarrhoea
(children should be kept off school for 48 hours following sickness or diarrhoea)
Religious observance
Service personnel – restricted leave
Trips out with the family
The alarm didn’t go off
The car wouldn’t start
Minor illness – runny nose/slight cold
Availability of cheap holidays
Someone else has organized a paid for holiday
Leave of Absence – There is a national threshold which is now in place and therefore from August 2024 the Department for Education has amended the Education (Pupil Registration) (England) Regulations 2006 removing the Headteacher’s ability to authorise leave of absence for a family holiday.
Herne Bay Infant and Nursery School – Attendance Policy – click here
Absence – If your child is unwell, please contact school before 9am letting us know the reason for absence. You can leave a message on our answer machine if you call before 8.30am.
If your child has a medical appointment, please let us know in advance providing/showing a copy of the appointment letter or text.
Punctuality Really Counts
School Day = 8.50am (gates open at 8.40am) – 3.05pm
Missing 30 minutes of school every day means missing:
2 ½ hours of school per week
95 hours of school per year
= nearly 4 weeks missed of school per year
Late marks (after 9.20am) in the register will count as an unauthorised absence for the morning. 10 unauthorised absences in 10 school weeks could result in a request for a Penalty Notice.
Why is being on time a good thing?
It sets positive patterns for the future.
It leads to good attendance.
It leads to better achievement.
It helps your child make friends and keep friends.
It gets your child’s day off to a good start.
Why is being late a bad thing?
It may lead to your child being confused all day as they may have missed information and instructions at the start of the day.
Can cause your child to fall behind with their work.
Can be embarrassing and get your child’s day off to a bad start.
Being late disrupts the lesson for everyone.
Some ideas that might help.
Make sure you have everything ready the night before e.g. book bag, swimming kit.
Make sure you allow plenty of time for you and your child to travel to school.
Establish a good bedtime and morning routine.
Get good rest and have a good routine yourself.
If you have difficulty getting your child into school on time, please talk to your child’s class teacher and ask for help. Remember it’s better to get help early on to stop little problems from becoming big ones!
From time to time you will meet Punctuality Parrot at one of our school gates, greeting children who arrive at school on time. Each week we celebrate arriving on time to school with a class certificate and stickers for the class who have the highest number of days where everyone arrives to school on time.

Herne Bay Infants and Nursery School governors are a committed team of volunteers, drawn from all walks of life, yet something we all share is having time, an open mind and a passion for education and the local community. The governing body is accountable for the school’s performance, its finances and the safety and well-being of pupils and staff. We support and challenge the school, ensuring it delivers the best education and environment possible.
If you are interested to know more about the governing body – flag one of us down, or send an email via the school to us.
Nicky Brown: Headteacher Governor
I have been a governor, in one guise or another, for over 20 years. Twice as a parent governor, once as a staff governor, once as a community governor and three times as a Headteacher … all but two of these was at an infant school. Governors have an important job ensuring that schools provide a high-quality education for its pupils within the budget that has been set and at Herne Bay Infant and Nursery School we have a talented and dedicated team of governors committed to getting our school to ‘outstanding’.
I joined Herne Bay Infant and Nursery School in 2021 from leading another school in Kent, however I spent a majority of my teaching career in Hampshire. I am proud to be the Headteacher of such a caring and forward-thinking school and I believe that our school has the potential to be the best in Herne Bay!

As an ‘incomer’, I felt keenly that I should make a contribution to the local community and so I was delighted when the opportunity to become a school governor arose.

Afterschool Club at Herne Bay Junior School.
The After School Club opened in 2010 and has become a very popular after school childcare facility. The club is run by our staff members Mrs Clare Ryder After School Club Supervisor, Mrs Paula Smith, Mrs Sam Deacon, Mrs Alison McKee, Mrs McMahon and Miss C. Findeis.
The children are provided with a wide range of activities each afternoon, these include board games, arts and crafts, puzzles, table football, stacking cups and dressing up. We also play outside where we have scooters, skipping and football for the children to use. Each child is provided with a snack and drink during each session. We have a selection of sandwiches and wraps while the weather is warm, as it gets colder, we serve hot food these are noodles, spaghetti hoops, baked beans, bagels, toast and crumpets. The children can have fresh fruit every day with their snack. We serve orange and blackcurrant squash and have hot chocolate as an extra in the colder months. Water is available at all times. If your child has any food intolerances of different dietary needs that we need to cater for please speak to Mrs Clare Ryder.
The After School Club runs from 3.05pm to 6pm Monday to Friday, term time only, at a cost of £8.00 per session, per child and is to be paid in advance. We are able to accept child care vouchers such as Eden Red, Computer Share, Busy Bees Benefits and Fideliti. We are Ofsted registered and our parents can claim up to 70% of the cost for child care provision through the Tax Credits scheme. Payment can be made through the School Money App.
If you have any queries or would like to book into After School Club (ASC) please email ASC@hernebay-jun.kent.sch.uk or cryder@hernebay-jun.kent.sch.uk you can also contact us by phone at 01227 374 2242 ext.2

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum - Herne Bay Infant and Nursery School
pageCache.text:
Believe in yourself, learn and never stop wanting to build a better world – Mary Mcleod Bethune.
Our curriculum content has been designed alongside subject leaders to take account of the legal requirements of the Early Years Foundations Stage (EYFS) Framework and the Primary National Curriculum whilst at the same time ensuring it meets the needs of all our children. It is ambitious, builds cultural capital and takes into account the context of our school locally.
Our community is at the heart of our teaching and learning and we have strong links with local organisations and community groups, such as Herne Bay Junior School, Christ Church St Andrews Church, Herne Bay library, Herons Leisure Centre and local museums. In addition to its coastal location, Herne Bay has a rich history which enriches children’s learning.
Our play and knowledge-based curriculum holds literature at its heart as we believe it is the key to exploring and making sense of the world around us, how events in the past shape our present and how current events may affect our future.
‘A child who reads will be an adult who thinks’ – proverb
At Herne Bay Infant and Nursery School our children in both our Nursery and Reception years follow the EYFS Framework. The Early Years is a vital stage for children as it helps prepare them for more formal teaching and lifelong learning. We want children’s early years’ experience to be a happy, active, exciting, fun and safe time which enables every individual child to achieve their full potential. We believe that that all children learn by ‘doing’ and our ambition is to embed our children in Nursery and Reception with a love of learning that they can take with them on their onward educational journey.
The skills and knowledge that our children acquire in the Early Years are consolidated and built upon through our Key Stage One curriculum. We strive to make our learning experiences relevant, practical and engaging, encouraging children to become independent thinkers. Our curriculum supports the school’s and British values and children are supported to strive for personal and academic success whilst respecting the thoughts and achievements of others.
Our curriculum reflects our increasingly diverse community, this diversity brings a richness to our school which we celebrate. We strive for all children to feel a sense of belonging within the school learning community and to develop an understanding of people, families and communities beyond their own.

Eligibility for Pupil Premium Funding
The government is currently allocating additional funding to schools in the form of ‘Pupil Premium’. If you are eligible for this funding your child may be entitled to additional support in school such as specialised support, subsidised clubs, and enrichment activities.
Although your child will be entitled to a Universal Infant Free School Meal in Year R – Year 2, it is important that you sign up to the Free School Meal funding scheme, to check whether you may be eligible for support. If you are eligible for Targeted Free School Meals, this will entitle your child to Pupil Premium, and will allow the school to offer targeted support. To be eligible for Free School Meal funding, you must be in receipt of Universal Credit. To be entitled to Targeted Free School Meal funding, and therefore Pupil Premium, your household income must also be below £7,400 per annum.

Pupil Premium at Herne Bay Infant School
Here at Herne Bay Infant School we use our pupil premium funding to diminish the difference in achievement of pupils eligible for pupil premium and other pupils. We ensure that the teaching and learning opportunities meet the needs of all pupils, and that appropriate provision is made for all pupils who belong to vulnerable groups. This includes ensuring that the needs of pupils who receive pupil premium funding are adequately assessed and addressed.

Pupil Premium Plus
In 2013 the DfE introduced Pupil Premium Plus for looked after and previously looked after children. In doing this, the DfE acknowledged the possible impact of trauma and loss in some children’s lives and the key role of schools in supporting children who have had a difficult start in life.
